title: Micro-Inference Slice Profiler for Tokenized Latency & Cache Attribution
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a lightweight, low-overhead profiler that emits fine-grained "token slice" events from the serving runtime. Each token-slice event will capture sequential micro-steps (prefix lookup, KV fetch, kernel compute, attention update, serialization) and a cache-hit flag so we can attribute latency and unit cost impact to cache behavior. The goal is a unified signal for performance analysis, regression detection, and cost-accuracy tradeoff experiments across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runtime emits token_slice events for >=95% of production requests in sampled mode with <3% p99 added latency overhead on a small canary GPU fleet.
2) Events include stable step names, durations (us), cache_hit boolean, model_version, route_id, request_id, and sequence_position.
3) Ingest pipeline stores events in the metrics lake with a nightly aggregation job producing per-route per-model token-latency histograms and cache-impact summaries.
4) Console dashboard shows: per-token mean/p95/p99 by step, cache-hit vs miss delta, and an ability to filter by model_version and rollout.
5) Alerting on regressions: >20% increase in p95 step latency for a route compared to baseline 
6) Backfill for last 30 days from sampled trace replay implemented in dev environment.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions:
- Emit minimal JSON-serialized events from the serving process to a local UDP collector for sampling, plus batched protobuf for high-throughput logs.
- Use adaptive sampling: always sample cold-starts and tail requests; probabilistic sample steady-state requests to keep cost predictable.
- Keep schema forward-compatible: step list as ordered array of short names and durations (us); cache_hit as single char flag.
- Prefer numeric microsecond timers from the runtime clock; include host kernel id for correlating with GPU-side traces.
- For Private deployments, provide opt-in config to redact PII and limit sample rate.
- Ensure scrubbing of customer prompt/response payloads; include only metadata and timings.
Implementation tasks:
- Runtime instrumentation patch (C++/Rust shim) to record micro-steps and emit event (ENG runtime team).
- Collector endpoint + lightweight agent (Go) to accept, batch, and forward to ingestion.
- Ingestion: new Kafka topic + schema registry entry, Avro/protobuf converters.
- Aggregation job (Spark/Beam) producing daily and hourly rollups.
- Console dashboard widgets and alert rules.
- E2E tests and performance benchmark harness.
- Docs: Confluence design + API spec + SDK docs for telemetry parsing.
telemetry_events:
Proposed token_slice schema (flattened):
- event_type: token_slice
- timestamp_iso
- request_id
- route_id
- model_version
- sequence_position (int)
- steps (comma-separated shortnames)
- durations_us (comma-separated integers matching step order)
- cache_hit (Y|N)
- host_id
- kernel_id
- sample_rate (float)
- truncated (Y|N)
Notes: store steps and durations as parallel CSV strings to avoid nested objects in early pipeline stages.
rollout_plan:
1) Implement runtime shim and unit tests in feature branch.
2) Canary deploy to internal-staging (5% traffic) with full sampling and perf counters.
3) Measure overhead and iterate to meet <3% p99 overhead target.
4) Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% sampling (adaptive) -> full production sampling model.
5) Enable console dashboard for internal SRE + product analytics teams.
6) Enable opt-in for select customers on Dedicated & Private after compliance review.
7) Post-launch: run a 30-day collection and validation, then schedule a reliability retro and ops runbook update.
